content.title: About
content.content: Egg white is the clear liquid separated from the yolk of a chicken egg. In frozen form it is pasteurized, which destroys pathogenic microorganisms while preserving its nutritional qualities. The product is convenient for cooking: it can be quickly thawed and used in baking, desserts, sauces, and protein shakes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg white is about 90 % water and the rest is protein, primarily albumin.
Pasteurization at 56–60 °C for a few minutes makes the product safe without major quality loss.
Frozen egg white can be stored up to 12 months at –18 °C while retaining most nutrients.
Its high foaming ability makes it ideal for creating stable meringues and soufflés.
Unlike whole eggs, egg white contains no cholesterol.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: One cup (≈240 ml) of frozen egg white provides about 26 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat and calories
items.content: 100 g of product contains less than 1 g of fat and roughly 50 kcal, making it suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Source of vitamin B2 (riboflavin)
items.content: Riboflavin is involved in energy metabolism and helps maintain healthy skin and eyes.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Egg white provides selenium, potassium and magnesium, important for antioxidant protection and nerve function.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Lysozyme and ovalbumin in egg white have antioxidant and antimicrobial properties.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People with egg allergy may react to pasteurized egg white, potentially experiencing severe symptoms.

items.title: Thawing safety
items.content: Improper thawing at room temperature can allow bacterial growth if the package is compromised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add a small amount of salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Thawed egg white can be beaten into stiff peaks for meringues, added to cake batters, made into yolk‑free omelets, blended into protein shakes, or used in sauces such as hollandaise.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen egg white in a sealed bag at –18 °C. After thawing, use within 24 hours, stored in the refrigerator (≤ 4 °C). Do not refreeze.
